title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Criminals used AI to create fake videos and social media profiles impersonating a real immigration attorney, charging vulnerable immigrants thousands of dollars for services never rendered. The scheme operated across multiple platforms, with scammers directing victims to contact numbers where they were presented with false contracts and promised assistance with US residency. The attorney discovered the fraud only when potential clients contacted his office, though the activity had been running for months before detection.

This is a case of impersonation enabled by AI-generated media. The deployment failure was social media platforms' lack of effective verification or account authentication to prevent fraudulent use of a real person's identity at scale. Catching this would have required either human review of new accounts claiming professional credentials, verification that the person in videos matched registered account holders, or cross-checking claimed credentials with actual practitioners.

It is not established who created or operated the scheme, what specific AI tools generated the videos, or whether the platforms had policies that would have prevented this if enforced.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an elaborate artificial intelligence fraud scheme. Criminals are creating hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using AI-generated images that impersonate Leal and offer immigration services he never provides. The scammers charge vulnerable immigrants thousands of dollars, including $2,200 for false promises of US residency assistance. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity started in October and has dramatically escalated over the past three months.

Working with an online anti-piracy company, Leal's office has removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically begin with social media videos directing people to contact a WhatsApp number, followed by phony contracts and false testimonials from supposed former clients. Leal warns immigrants to watch for requests for payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the source of the fraud.
